subject: Brightleaf Observability: Dashboard & Runbook Handoff
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightleafhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@brightleafhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Brightleaf observability kickoff / owners

Ben / Laura —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Per our internal kickoff, we want to confirm owners and the minimum scope for the first observability handoff: dashboards, tracing hooks for the payments/service APIs, an error taxonomy to feed alert rules, and a 30-day on-call routing plan while our SRE team finishes playbook edits.

Can you confirm:
- Which Redwood person will drive the dashboard build and initial alerts?
- Will Redwood provide a runbook template and a draft runbook we can edit?
- Any recommended thresholds for high-rate 5xx and latency p95 to start with?

We’d like to get a draft runbook and dashboard list by Monday (13th) if possible. Attaching our current dashboard inventory (CSV) for your reference.

Thanks,
Sara Liu
Head of Site Reliability
Brightleaf Health
attachments: brightleaf_initial_dashboard_list.csv (CSV)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightleafhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightleaf observability kickoff / owners

Sara —

Appreciate the inventory; that helps. Quick replies to your bullets and a proposed plan below.

Owners (proposed):
- Dashboard + initial Grafana templates: Ben Carter (PM, onboarding) with Laura as escalation owner.
- Tracing hooks & sampling recommendations: Marissa Cole (Instrumentation lead).
- Runbook template + draft: Ben + Jonas Weber (SRE partner) — we’ll drop a draft for you to edit.

Minimum scope (what we’ll deliver in the first handoff):
- 6 curated dashboards: service health, payments latency, error budget, user-facing latencies, queue depth, and infra GPU/utilization.
- Tracing hook checklist for payments/service APIs (patch attached for suggested instrumentation points).
- Error taxonomy doc mapping common Brightleaf errors to Alert categories (sev1, sev2, sev3) with remediation links.
- A starter runbook (RBW_Runbook_template_v2.docx) prefilled with on-call routing and escalation steps.

Threshold recommendations (starting point):
- 5xx rate: >= 0.5% over 5m across payment API endpoints -> create paged alert (adjust per endpoint).
- p95 latency: > 750ms over 5m for payment authorization -> page.
- Error budget burn: > 5% in 1h -> precedence alert (email + Slack, not page immediately).

Timeline / deliverables:
- Draft dashboard list + runbook: Mon 2027-09-13 EOD (we’ll upload to the Drive link and attach doc).
- Instrumentation checklist + tracing patch: Mon 2027-09-13 morning.
- First pass alerts wired into your Slack channel (test mode) by Wed 2027-09-15.

Can you confirm the on-call rotation you want Redwood to route to for the 30-day interim? If you prefer, Redwood can queue alerts to your Ops Slack channel and have our SREs act as primary for P1s for the first 30 days (we’ll capture all actions in the runbook).

I’ve attached the runbook template and the tracing hooks patch.

—
Ben Carter
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
attachments: RBW_Runbook_template_v2.docx (DOCX), Brightleaf_Redwood_Tracing_hooks.patch (PATCH)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightleafhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightleaf observability kickoff / owners

Sara —

Adding a bit more structure from the operations side to make the handoff executable. I’m dropping the dashboard owner and a mapping of what each dashboard will show so your dashboards team can review:

Dashboard ownership (Redwood -> Brightleaf transfer plan):
- Payments overview (owner: Ben) — transaction rate, p50/p95, 5xx per endpoint, success flows.
- Authorization traces (owner: Marissa) — sample spans around auth, DB calls, downstream service calls.
- Error taxonomy dashboard (owner: Laura) — classification counts by error code mapped to remediation playbook.
- K8s infra health (owner: Jonas) — node CPU, OOMs, restarts; alert when node restarts > 3 in 15m.
- User-perf heatmap (owner: Ben) — slow paths by region and endpoint.
- Queue depth & retry errors (owner: Marissa) — backpressure signals.

Runbook comments: we’ll prefill playbook entries for the top 5 P1 flows and link to runbooks for downstream services. Please confirm the people to page for P1 (email/Slack handles) — if you want Redwood to be the primary responder for P1s during the 30-day ramp, we’ll need a signed change of operations agreement (I can send the short form now).

I’ll put the dashboard mockups into the Drive folder and add a sample alert routing matrix (who to page for which alert).

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightleafhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@brightleafhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightleaf observability kickoff / owners

Thanks Ben/Laura — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. Quick answers:
- For the 30-day interim we’d like Redwood to act as primary for P1 pages (Brightleaf will shadow and take over after the 30-day window). Please send over the short operations agreement and we’ll review in procurement.
- Our on-call P1 contact will be: ops-oncall@brightleafhealth.com (this routes to the platform team pager). For P2s please route to ops-silent-alerts@brightleafhealth.com.
- We prefer the thresholds you suggested as a starting point; Marissa will validate sampling rates for traces.

Deliverables requested: draft runbook + dashboard list by EOD 9/13 (we understand timing was tight — if any delay, flag it). Also please mark any alerts you will initially suppress while we stabilize (so we can avoid noisy paging).

We’ll expect the initial test alerts in Slack channel #brightleaf-ops-test.

—
Sara Liu
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightleafhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightleaf observability kickoff / owners

Sara —

Great — thanks for the confirmations. Summary of next steps (action owners & dates):
1) Ben — upload draft runbook (RBW_Runbook_template_v2.docx) + dashboard list to Drive by Tue 2027-09-14 17:00 PT.
2) Marissa — deliver tracing hook checklist and suggested sampling config by Tue 2027-09-14 12:00 PT.
3) Laura & Jonas — populate alert routing matrix and suppression list; provide recommended paging windows by Wed 2027-09-15 09:00 PT.
4) Redwood Ops — wire test alerts to #brightleaf-ops-test (Slack) in test mode by Wed 2027-09-15 EOD.
5) Sara / Brightleaf — confirm procurement sign-off for 30-day Redwood P1 coverage; if signed, send ops-oncall alias and escalation contacts.

I will also open SUP-2345 to track the handoff items and share it with your team. If anything slips we’ll call out scope changes immediately.

Thanks — we’ll follow up with the Drive links once the docs are uploaded.

—
Ben Carter
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
